summary: Gemma 4 26B-A4B UD-Q4_K_XL decode-attention kernel result on RX 7900 XTX: the same four-row separated-phase matrix re-measured on the same day, hardware, artifact and frozen prompt ids as the G0 baseline, after the bit-exact barrier-batched decode attention kernel landed (hipengine commit 50e9258f7). Decode 16.093 -> 20.418 tok/s at 1024/128 (+26.9%); shape matrix decode 33.96 / 26.56 / 20.42 / 11.71 tok/s vs baseline 32.25 / 22.02 / 16.09 / 10.14; prefill and first-token latency unchanged within noise; public-path token-id parity exact on every row.
execution_profile_note: The gemma4 GGUF path resolved no execution-profile override (resolved_execution_profile=None); registered strict unfused fallbacks per the fused-kernel invariant. Profile-schema fields are intentionally null rather than asserted.

generated_id_equality.evidence: instrumented runner rows match untouched LLM.generate() token ids at every position on all 4 measured rows (public_path_parity=true); the decode kernel itself is bit-exact with the pre-change block kernel per 83 bitwise parity tests in tests/test_gpu_gemma4_attention_decode_parity.py

measurements.boundary_note: Boundary and capacity rows were measured on the pre-kernel baseline artifact (2026-09-24-gemma4-26b-a4b-g0-baseline.json) and are not re-measured here: the decode kernel changes no routing decision or token count, its arithmetic is bit-identical to the previous decode path, and all four re-measured rows keep exact public-path token-id parity against the same frozen prompt ids. Boundary rates are re-established in the campaign integrated confirmation phase; they were never headline numbers.

conventions.decode_tps: (outputs - 1) / predicted_ms; predicted_ms also spans the first greedy sample

qwen36_35b_a3b_shipping_route.note: different-model product reference with its own tokenizer; prompt content is engine-local by campaign rule. Default-route run (no --public-ar-profile) measured decode 114.13 tok/s and prefers the slower non-shipping prefill route.

campaign_target.definition: Gemma median decode tok/s at 1024 prompt / 128 output >= 70% of the Qwen3.6-35B-A3B shipping-route reference at the same workload

decision.reason: decode-attention kernel validated before measurement: 83 bitwise prefill-vs-decode parity tests, gemma4 unit/GPU suites exit 0, default tier limited to its two pre-existing recorded failures, GPUs idle, worktree clean at 50e9258f7. All four rows public-path parity exact; prefill unchanged (noise); decode +26.9% at 1024/128 and positive at every measured shape.

limitations: Same measurement session day, host, GPU, artifact and frozen prompt ids as the G0 baseline artifact, which supplies the paired baseline decode rows in measurements.baseline_reference.
Boundary and capacity rows were not re-measured (see measurements.boundary_note).
llama.cpp comparator rows are re-used from the baseline session as the fixed same-GPU basis; they are unchanged, and hipEngine-side deltas are what this artifact measures.

Decode gain is shape-dependent: +5.3% at 128-prompt vs +26.9% at 1024-prompt, because attention share grows with live keys; the remaining gap to the 80.20 tok/s target needs the linears, host work and pack8 candidates.
A second independent 1024/128 validation run before this matrix measured 20.484 tok/s; this artifact reports only its own four runs (20.418 median).
note: Engine change under measurement: hipengine commit 50e9258f7 (bit-exact barrier-batched decode attention kernel; design history in worklog entry 20260924T102206.088801Z-lhl-gemma4-a651b0.md). Raw per-run harness artifacts lived in /tmp during the session; this file consolidates their stats and parity flags. Workload and hardware fields are inherited from the baseline artifact and identical for these runs.
